candidates.title: The arterial-calcification score may be reading inspiratory depth
candidates.question: Is CT-CLIP's arterial-wall-calcification output using normalized diaphragm dome height as an image cue?
candidates.deliverable_sentence: The model is using normalized diaphragm dome height as an image cue for arterial wall calcification.
candidates.kernel_provenance: The kernel comes from the pitch's asserted score collapse after changing the left hemidiaphragm and its proposed monotonic response to dome translation; the mortality, slice-wise, longitudinal, and numerical claims were discarded as unverified.

X_measurement.X: Normalized diaphragm dome height, measured separately for each hemidiaphragm as the craniocaudal apex-to-dome distance divided by thoracic craniocaudal length, with total segmented lung volume as a companion inspiratory-depth measure.
X_measurement.how: Automatically segment the lungs, identify the most caudal point of each lung-diaphragm interface and the ipsilateral lung apex in physical coordinates, and divide their distance by thoracic length. The calculation is deterministic and can be repeated after the model's exact preprocessing.
X_measurement.could_compute_today_without_asking_anyon: Yes. It is a geometric measurement over automated masks and voxel coordinates; no reader label is required.

candidates.suspected_signal: Inspiratory depth changes diaphragm position, lung volume, and the craniocaudal arrangement of thoracic anatomy. A volume classifier trained on report-derived labels could therefore use this global respiratory-state cue as a correlate of the population in which arterial calcification is reported, rather than localizing calcified plaque.
candidates.keystone_prerequisite: A plaque-preserving counterfactual can change normalized diaphragm dome height across the natural NLST range while keeping every aortic and other hyperattenuating voxel, final-tensor framing, and local image texture unchanged enough that matched sham edits are indistinguishable from the active edit.
candidates.keystone_evidence: The official CT-CLIP repository states that pretrained CT-CLIP variants and inference code are released and that inference can run on smaller GPUs (official repository: https://github.com/ibrahimethemhamamci/CT-CLIP). The official TCIA NLST collection page lists public CT images under CC BY 4.0 (https://www.cancerimagingarchive.net/collection/nlst/). These verify the adjacent model/data facts, not the load-bearing counterfactual-validity conjunction.
candidates.keystone_residual_assumption: If I have only verified the nearest checkable thing, what am I still assuming? I verified that the model family, inference path, and public scans exist; I am still assuming that diaphragm height can be changed without the model responding to boundary warping, altered lung shape, or crop/framing changes. That is the real keystone.
candidates.use_vs_association_design: Hold the original aorta and all calcified voxels exactly fixed, apply a bidirectional dose series of diaphragm-height edits, and require a larger ordered output response than equal-energy pleural-boundary and spatially shifted sham edits; an observational score-X correlation is exploratory only.

dataset.primary: National Lung Screening Trial low-dose chest CT collection on The Cancer Imaging Archive (NLST; TCIA)
dataset.access: Public imaging collection, CC BY 4.0; use a small prespecified sample without relying on restricted clinical outcomes.

candidates.smallest_decisive_experiment: Select 32 NLST noncontrast inspiratory CT volumes spanning the natural diaphragm-height distribution and containing both low and high automated thoracic-aortic calcium burden. Run one frozen CT-CLIP arterial-wall-calcification output. For each scan, create two or three small cranial and caudal diaphragm-boundary displacements confined to a thin caudal lung band while copying the entire aorta, heart, spine, all voxels above 130 HU, and the final crop coordinates unchanged. Compare paired output slopes against equal-energy lateral-pleural, left-right-swapped, and phase-scrambled displacement shams. Preregister a natural-range X change, a sham-effect ceiling, and an output-equivalence margin. Batched inference over fewer than 300 volumes fits one Colab GPU session; counterfactual construction is CPU-side.

closest_prior_work.citation: Hamamci et al., A foundation model utilizing chest CT volumes and radiology reports for supervised-level zero-shot detection of abnormalities
closest_prior_work.verified_fact: CT-CLIP performs volume-level multi-abnormality detection from 3D chest CT and its official repository provides inference code and pretrained-model links.
closest_prior_work.delta: The primary paper did not test whether its arterial-wall-calcification output uses diaphragm position.

closest_prior_work.citation: Bak et al., Automated evaluation of diaphragm configuration based on chest CT in COPD patients
closest_prior_work.verified_fact: An automated CT diaphragm index was measured in 8,431 COPDGene participants and was associated with COPD severity, FEV1 percent predicted, and emphysema score.
closest_prior_work.delta: This establishes computable diaphragm geometry, not use by a calcification classifier.

closest_prior_work.citation: van Velzen et al., Deep Learning for Automatic Calcium Scoring in CT: Validation Using Multiple Cardiac CT and Chest CT Protocols
closest_prior_work.verified_fact: A location-aware deep-learning method quantified coronary and thoracic-aortic calcification across multiple noncontrast CT protocols.
closest_prior_work.delta: It provides a local-calcium comparator and shows that anatomically grounded scoring is feasible; it did not audit CT-CLIP or diaphragm reliance.

candidates.novelty_statement: NO NOVELTY CLAIM. A bounded primary-source search found the CT-CLIP model paper, quantitative diaphragm work, and automated thoracic-calcium work, but not this specific causal audit; human verification is still required.
candidates.critical_confound: The active edit may create an unnatural lung-diaphragm boundary or alter global lung shape/framing, so a positive result could reflect sensitivity to synthetic geometry rather than native use of inspiratory depth.

alternative_explanations.alternative: CT-CLIP responds to interpolation or boundary seams.
alternative_explanations.control: Equal-energy lateral-pleural and phase-scrambled boundary shams, multiple interpolation kernels, and a blinded active-versus-sham edit discriminator.

alternative_explanations.alternative: The edit changes lung volume or crop occupancy rather than diaphragm height.
alternative_explanations.control: Match final-tensor framing exactly and either preserve total lung volume with local compensation or estimate diaphragm-height and lung-volume effects separately in a factorial edit.

alternative_explanations.alternative: The output is driven by actual calcium or reconstruction noise.
alternative_explanations.control: Copy all hyperattenuating and aortic voxels bit-for-bit, stratify by automated calcium burden and reconstruction metadata, and use only within-volume comparisons.

standing_confounds_addressed.scanner_vendor_protocol_reconstruction_s: Held fixed within each edited volume; stratified replication tests effect stability but does not establish broad generalization.
standing_confounds_addressed.patient_positioning: The source scan and crop are fixed; native positioning cannot explain paired changes, although the edit may resemble a positioning artifact.
standing_confounds_addressed.disease_prevalence_and_referral_pathway: Cannot cause paired output changes, but could explain why a model learned the cue and limits interpretation.
standing_confounds_addressed.label_leakage_from_report: No report or label enters the primary paired readout; report-derived training labels could still explain why the shortcut was learned.

anticipated_negative.reason: If validated edits span the natural diaphragm-height range, the model responds to a positive control, sham effects remain below threshold, and the arterial-wall-calcification output remains within a preregistered equivalence margin, appreciable use of this defined X is weakened. If edit-validity gates fail, the result is uninterpretable and is not counted as a negative.

rung.move_up: A validated plaque-preserving perturbation can reach rung 1. Replication across reconstruction/vendor strata and rejection of framing artifacts gates rung 2. Only then does the named normalized diaphragm-height sentence qualify as rung 3; the experiment does not establish why the association was learned or any mortality effect.

candidates.dies_like_prior: It most closely resembles idea-006 because a large synthetic intervention could be out of distribution, and idea-007 because respiratory state co-varies with final-tensor framing. It differs by prohibiting patient deletion, using small natural-range bidirectional boundary edits, preserving plaque voxels, and making sham/distribution gates prerequisites. It still dies the same way if those gates fail. Annotation provenance does not apply because X and the primary readout are computed without labels.

clarity.why: One released model output, one geometric X, and one directional paired test are specified.

identifiability.why: Plaque-preserving paired edits rule out patient-level confounds, but separating diaphragm height from synthetic boundary and lung-shape effects remains difficult.

medical_relevance.why: It could expose a clinically misleading respiratory-state shortcut in an arterial-calcification output, but it does not itself improve calcium quantification or outcomes.

interest.why: A calcification score driven by respiratory geometry would be surprising and consequential for interpretation.

prior_legwork.why: Model code/weights, public CT, quantitative diaphragm geometry, and automated thoracic-calcium comparators exist.

feasibility.why: Capped because counterfactual validity is not inspected; the small inference workload otherwise fits one Colab GPU session.

data_readiness.why: NLST CT images are publicly listed by TCIA and the primary test needs neither outcomes nor manual annotations.

evaluation_readiness.why: Paired slope, sham ceiling, equivalence margin, X range, and voxel-preservation checks are definable before inference.

negative_result_value.why: After all sensitivity and edit-validity gates pass, equivalence directly weakens use of this X.

novelty_confidence.why: Capped by the uninspected keystone and a bounded rather than exhaustive primary-source search.

regret.why: The first gated test is small and could cheaply falsify a striking shortcut hypothesis.

unverified_claims: The current released CT-CLIP checkpoint and label mapping expose the exact arterial-wall-calcification output reproducibly.
Natural-range diaphragm-height edits can pass the declared distribution and sham gates.
The defined output uses diaphragm height in intact unedited scans.
No prior study has performed this exact causal audit.
prohibited_conclusions: Do not call the output an aortic-specific head without verifying the released label mapping.
Do not infer that CT-CLIP contains separate slice-wise and volume-wise detectors.
Do not infer mortality prediction, sign inversion, longitudinal drift, or causation from smoking or COPD.
Do not interpret a failed edit-validity gate as a negative result.
